question.problem:
Find the sum modulo $24$ of the solutions to the congruence $20x≡12\,(\text{mod}\,24).$

*Hint: You may wish to use trial and error to find the appropriate multiplicative inverse.*
question.worked_solution:
In the given congruence, we have $a=20$ and $n=24$, and so

$$
\text{gcd}(a,n)=\text{gcd}(20,24)=4.
$$

Since $b=12$ is divisible by $4,$ our congruence has $4$ solutions.

First, we use the division property of congruences:

$$
\begin{aligned}20x & ≡12 &  & (\text{mod}\,24) \\ 4\cdot 5x & ≡4\cdot 3 &  & (\text{mod}\,4\cdot 6) \\ \cancel{4}\cdot 5x & ≡\cancel{4}\cdot 3 &  & (\text{mod}\,\cancel{4}\cdot 6) \\ 5x & ≡3 &  & (\text{mod}\,6)\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that in the new congruence, we have ${a}_{1}=5$ and ${n}_{1}=6$, where

$$
\text{gcd}({a}_{1},{n}_{1})=\text{gcd}(5,6)=1.
$$

So, our congruence has a unique solution modulo $6.$

To find the solution, we need to multiply both sides of the equation by the multiplicative inverse of $5\,(\text{mod}\,6).$ To find the inverse of $5\,(\text{mod}\,6),$ we compute the exponents of $6\,(\text{mod}\,10)$ until we get a result of $1\,(\text{mod}\,6):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{5}^{2}≡25≡4\cdot 6+1≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,6)\end{aligned}
$$

So, $5\cdot 5≡1\,(\text{mod}\,6),$ which means that $5$ is the multiplicative inverse of $5$ (modulo $6$).

Now, multiplying both sides of our congruence by $5,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}5x & ≡3 &  & (\text{mod}\,6) \\ 5\cdot 5x & ≡5\cdot 3 &  & (\text{mod}\,6) \\ (5\cdot 5)x & ≡15 &  & (\text{mod}\,6) \\ x & ≡15 &  & (\text{mod}\,6) \\ x & ≡2\cdot 6+3 &  & (\text{mod}\,6) \\ x & ≡3 &  & (\text{mod}\,6)\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get the solution $x≡3\,(\text{mod}\,6).$ 

But our original congruence was modulo $24$ (not modulo $6$). To find all the solutions modulo $24,$ we repeatedly add $6$ modulo $24$ until we reach the number $3$ again:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ≡3 &  & (\text{mod}\,24) \\ {x}_{2} & ≡3+6≡9 &  & (\text{mod}\,24) \\ {x}_{3} & ≡9+6≡15 &  & (\text{mod}\,24) \\ {x}_{4} & ≡15+6≡21 &  & (\text{mod}\,24) \\ {x}_{5} & ≡21+6≡27≡24+3≡3≡{x}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,24)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $x≡3,9,15,21\,(\text{mod}\,24).$ 

Finally,

$$
3+9+15+21≡48≡2\cdot 24≡0\,(\text{mod}\,24).
$$
